question: 1) Consider $\triangle ABC$ with right angle at C and $m(\angle ABC) = 55^{\circ}$. If the length of $\overline{AC}$ is 10 units, then what is the area of the triangle? (Given $\tan 35^{\circ} \approx 0.7$ and $\tan 55^{\circ} \approx 1.43$)
explanation: Let $b$ be the side opposite $\angle B$, and $a$ be the side opposite $\angle A$. $C$ is the right angle, so $c$ is the hypotenuse. We are given $AC = b = 10$ and $m(\angle B) = 55^{\circ}$. Since $C=90^{\circ}$, then $m(\angle A) = 90^{\circ} - 55^{\circ} = 35^{\circ}$. The area of the triangle is $Area = \frac{1}{2}ab$. We need the length of the side $BC=a$. We can use the tangent function with $\angle A$: $\tan A = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}} = \frac{a}{b}$. So, $\tan 35^{\circ} = \frac{a}{10}$. $a = 10 \times \tan 35^{\circ} \approx 10 \times 0.7 = 7$. The area is $Area = \frac{1}{2} \times a \times b = \frac{1}{2} \times 7 \times 10 = 35$ sq. units. (Using $\tan B = \frac{b}{a}$: $\tan 55^{\circ} = \frac{10}{a}$. $a = \frac{10}{\tan 55^{\circ}} \approx \frac{10}{1.43} \approx 6.99$, which also gives an area $\approx 35$).
